text:
A keloid is a raised, firm scar that grows beyond the edges of the original wound because the body lays down too much collagen during healing. The team note has this backwards: too little collagen would give a flat, faint scar, not a keloid. Keloids don't regress on their own, often recur after simple excision, and are more common in darker skin, typically on the earlobes, chest, shoulders and upper back.
